accepted.s: The Indo-Soviet Treaty of Peace, Friendship and Cooperation was signed on:
accepted.x: The Indo-Soviet Treaty of Peace, Friendship and Cooperation was signed on 9 August 1971.
accepted.tq: Use the precise date rather than the related Bangladesh War dates.
accepted.sec: 1971-1991 - Indo-Soviet Treaty, Bangladesh, Simla, Farakka, Pokhran-I, IPKF  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Indo-Soviet Treaty of 1971 was primarily signed in the context of:
o: The 1962 war with China and the NPT negotiations
The Kargil War and the Lahore Declaration
The 1991 economic crisis and the collapse of the USSR
The Bangladesh crisis and the US-China-Pakistan alignment
accepted.x: The treaty was signed to counter the US-China-Pakistan axis during the Bangladesh crisis.
accepted.tq: Identify the immediate strategic context behind the agreement.
accepted.sec: 1971-1991 - Indo-Soviet Treaty, Bangladesh, Simla, Farakka, Pokhran-I, IPKF  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was an important consequence of the Indo-Soviet Treaty of 1971 for India?
o: It required India to join a formal military alliance against China
It provided a security umbrella along with increased Soviet arms and aid
It transferred the administration of East Pakistan to India
It ended India’s policy of non-alignment
accepted.x: The treaty gave India a security umbrella and facilitated greater Soviet arms and aid. It did not formally end non-alignment or create a military alliance.
accepted.tq: Distinguish strategic support from a formal military alliance.
accepted.sec: 1971-1991 - Indo-Soviet Treaty, Bangladesh, Simla, Farakka, Pokhran-I, IPKF  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the Bangladesh Liberation War, consider the following statements:
1. East Pakistan broke away and Bangladesh emerged as an independent country.
2. Pakistan’s army surrendered in Dhaka on 16 December 1971.
3. The war took place in December 1971.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Bangladesh emerged from the break-up of East Pakistan, and Pakistan’s army surrendered in Dhaka on 16 December 1971.
accepted.tq: Check all three linked facts of the event before selecting the complete combination.
accepted.sec: 1971-1991 - Indo-Soviet Treaty, Bangladesh, Simla, Farakka, Pokhran-I, IPKF  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Simla Agreement of 1972 is associated with which principle?
o: Bilateralism and exclusion of a third-party role
Joint control of the Ganga waters by India and Nepal
Internationalisation of the Kashmir issue through the United Nations
accepted.x: The Simla Agreement emphasised bilateralism and ruled out a third-party role in resolving India-Pakistan issues.
accepted.tq: Match the agreement with its distinctive diplomatic principle.
accepted.sec: 1971-1991 - Indo-Soviet Treaty, Bangladesh, Simla, Farakka, Pokhran-I, IPKF  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Farakka Accord of 1977 concerned:
o: Sharing of Ganga waters between India and Bangladesh
The demarcation of the India-Sri Lanka maritime boundary
The settlement of the Kashmir dispute
Sharing of Indus waters between India and Pakistan
accepted.x: The 1977 Farakka Accord dealt with Ganga water sharing between India and Bangladesh.
accepted.tq: Separate water-sharing agreements from political and maritime agreements.
accepted.sec: 1971-1991 - Indo-Soviet Treaty, Bangladesh, Simla, Farakka, Pokhran-I, IPKF  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Pokhran-I, conducted on 18 May 1974, was officially described as a:
accepted.x: India described the 18 May 1974 Pokhran-I test as a peaceful nuclear explosion.
accepted.tq: Use the exact official description attached to the event.
accepted.sec: 1971-1991 - Indo-Soviet Treaty, Bangladesh, Simla, Farakka, Pokhran-I, IPKF  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following followed Pokhran-I?
o: International concern and tighter global nuclear controls
The signing of the 123 Agreement with the United States
accepted.x: Pokhran-I generated international concern and led to tighter global nuclear controls. The other developments occurred much later.
accepted.tq: Identify the immediate international consequence rather than a later nuclear event.
accepted.sec: 1971-1991 - Indo-Soviet Treaty, Bangladesh, Simla, Farakka, Pokhran-I, IPKF  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Indian Peace Keeping Force was deployed in Sri Lanka during:
accepted.x: The IPKF operated in Sri Lanka from 1987 to 1990 under the India-Sri Lanka Accord of 1987.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the deployment period from the year in which the accord was signed.
accepted.sec: 1971-1991 - Indo-Soviet Treaty, Bangladesh, Simla, Farakka, Pokhran-I, IPKF  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The India-Sri Lanka Accord of 1987 was signed by:
o: Atal Bihari Vajpayee and Nawaz Sharif
P.V. Narasimha Rao and Chandrika Kumaratunga
accepted.x: The 1987 India-Sri Lanka Accord was associated with Rajiv Gandhi and Sri Lankan President J.R. Jayewardene.
accepted.tq: Apply the wrong-person-with-the-deed trap to bilateral agreements.
accepted.sec: 1971-1991 - Indo-Soviet Treaty, Bangladesh, Simla, Farakka, Pokhran-I, IPKF  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Katchatheevu — Ceded to Sri Lanka in 1974
accepted.x: Indira Gandhi was assassinated in 1984, whereas Rajiv Gandhi was assassinated in 1991. The other pairs are correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped year in an otherwise familiar set of associations.

accepted.s:
Match the following agreements with their parties or signatories:

List-I
 a. Tashkent Declaration
 b. Indo-Soviet Treaty
 c. Simla Agreement
 d. Lahore Declaration

List-II
 i. India–USSR
 ii. Shastri–Ayub Khan
 iii. Vajpayee–Nawaz Sharif
 iv. Indira Gandhi–Z.A. Bhutto

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: Tashkent involved Shastri and Ayub Khan; the Indo-Soviet Treaty involved India and the USSR; Simla involved Indira Gandhi and Z.A. Bhutto; Lahore involved Vajpayee and Nawaz Sharif.
accepted.tq: Use the parties to distinguish agreements with closely related India-Pakistan contexts.

accepted.s: The Ganga Waters Treaty between India and Bangladesh was concluded in:
accepted.x: The Ganga Waters Treaty with Bangladesh was concluded in 1996 and was for a period of 30 years.
accepted.tq: Separate the later treaty from the earlier Farakka Accord by year and duration.
accepted.sec: Treaties and agreements → year, parties, chronology  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following represents the correct chronological order?
o: Tashkent Declaration → Indo-Soviet Treaty → Simla Agreement → Farakka Accord
Indo-Soviet Treaty → Tashkent Declaration → Farakka Accord → Simla Agreement
Simla Agreement → Tashkent Declaration → Indo-Soviet Treaty → Farakka Accord
Farakka Accord → Simla Agreement → Indo-Soviet Treaty → Tashkent Declaration
accepted.x: The correct order is 1966 Tashkent, 1971 Indo-Soviet Treaty, 1972 Simla and 1977 Farakka.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the middle agreements.
accepted.sec: Treaties and agreements → year, parties, chronology  [other exams]

accepted.s: Pokhran-II was conducted on:
accepted.x: Pokhran-II, known as Operation Shakti, was conducted on 11 and 13 May 1998 under Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the two 1998 test dates from the single date of Pokhran-I.
accepted.sec: Post-1998 - Pokhran-II, NFU, sanctions, Lahore, Kargil, nuclear deal, NSG waiver  [other exams]

accepted.s: Operation Shakti resulted in India declaring itself a:
o: Signatory to the NPT as a nuclear-weapon state
Permanent member of the UN Security Council
Member of the Nuclear Suppliers Group
accepted.x: Following Pokhran-II, India declared itself a nuclear-weapon state. India did not become an NPT-recognised nuclear-weapon state or an NSG member through the tests.
accepted.tq: Reject status claims that confuse a national declaration with international treaty recognition.
accepted.sec: Post-1998 - Pokhran-II, NFU, sanctions, Lahore, Kargil, nuclear deal, NSG waiver  [other exams]

accepted.s: India’s No First Use policy was formally adopted in:
accepted.x: Although announced by the Vajpayee government after Pokhran-II, the No First Use doctrine was formally adopted in 2003.
accepted.tq: Separate the announcement year from the year of formal adoption.

accepted.s: Which of the following countries was associated with sanctions imposed after India’s 1998 nuclear tests?
accepted.x: The United States, under the Glenn Amendment, Japan and others imposed sanctions after the nuclear tests.
accepted.tq: Identify the country and legal instrument directly connected with the sanctions.

o: The signing of the Simla Agreement
The sanctions imposed after India’s nuclear tests
accepted.x: The Jaswant Singh–Strobe Talbott talks followed the sanctions imposed after India’s 1998 nuclear tests.

accepted.s: The Lahore Declaration of February 1999 was accompanied by:
accepted.x: The Lahore Declaration came with the Delhi–Lahore bus diplomacy in February 1999.
accepted.tq: Associate the declaration with its accompanying diplomatic initiative.
accepted.sec: Post-1998 - Pokhran-II, NFU, sanctions, Lahore, Kargil, nuclear deal, NSG waiver  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which statement about the Kargil War of 1999 is correct?
o: It occurred before both countries conducted nuclear tests and ended through Soviet mediation.
It was settled by the Farakka Accord and involved Bangladesh as a principal party.
It led directly to the signing of the Indo-Soviet Treaty.
It was the first conflict after India and Pakistan had tested nuclear weapons, and US pressure forced Pakistan to withdraw.
accepted.x: The Kargil War was the first conflict after both India and Pakistan had tested nuclear weapons; US pressure contributed to Pakistan’s withdrawal.
accepted.tq: Combine the event’s timing with its decisive diplomatic consequence.
accepted.sec: Post-1998 - Pokhran-II, NFU, sanctions, Lahore, Kargil, nuclear deal, NSG waiver  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Indo-US civil nuclear deal:
1. A joint statement was issued in 2005.
2. The Hyde Act was enacted in 2006.
3. The NSG waiver was granted on 6 September 2008.
4. The 123 Agreement was signed in October 2008.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct and represent the principal milestones of the Indo-US civil nuclear deal.
accepted.tq: Track a multi-stage agreement through its successive dates.

accepted.s: The 123 Agreement was signed between:
o: India and the Nuclear Suppliers Group
accepted.x: The 123 Agreement was the Indo-US civil nuclear agreement signed in October 2008.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the bilateral agreement from the separate NSG waiver.

accepted.s: The NSG waiver for India was granted on:
accepted.x: The Nuclear Suppliers Group waiver was granted to India on 6 September 2008; the 123 Agreement followed in October 2008.
accepted.tq: Separate the waiver date from the date of the subsequent bilateral agreement.

accepted.s: According to the phase classification of India’s foreign policy, the period 1998–2013 represented India as a:
accepted.x: The period 1998–2013 is identified as the phase of India as a “balancing power.”

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the first phase of India’s foreign policy, 1946–1962?
accepted.x: The 1946–1962 phase is described as optimistic non-alignment, marked by idealism, Panchsheel, NAM, Commonwealth membership and anti-imperialism.
accepted.tq: Use the exact phase label rather than a related policy instrument.
accepted.sec: Nehruvian era - NAM, Korean War role, 1962 impact

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT a feature associated with the Nehruvian phase of foreign policy?
o: Formal alignment with a Cold War military bloc
accepted.x: The Nehruvian phase emphasised Panchsheel, non-alignment, Commonwealth membership and anti-imperialism; it did not involve formal alignment with a Cold War military bloc.
accepted.tq: Identify the option that contradicts the central principle of non-alignment.
accepted.sec: Nehruvian era - NAM, Korean War role, 1962 impact

accepted.s: In relation to the Korean War, India chaired the:
o: Neutral Nations Repatriation Commission for prisoners of war
United Nations Security Council committee on sanctions
South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation council
accepted.x: India chaired the Neutral Nations Repatriation Commission for prisoners of war during the Korean War, with General K.S. Thimayya associated with it.
accepted.tq: Match the country’s diplomatic role with the exact international body.
accepted.sec: Nehruvian era - NAM, Korean War role, 1962 impact

accepted.s: General K.S. Thimayya was associated with India’s role in the Korean War as:
o: Commander of the IPKF in Sri Lanka
Chairman of the NSG waiver committee
Chairman of the Neutral Nations Repatriation Commission for prisoners of war
India’s representative in the Indo-Soviet Treaty negotiations
accepted.x: General K.S. Thimayya was associated with India’s chairmanship of the Neutral Nations Repatriation Commission for prisoners of war.
accepted.tq: Apply the person-to-role matching method in an international context.
accepted.sec: Nehruvian era - NAM, Korean War role, 1962 impact

accepted.s: After the Korean War, India’s relations with the Soviet Union warmed partly because of Soviet:
o: Food aid, veto on Kashmir and support over Goa
Support for India’s entry into NATO and the European Union
Mediation in the Kargil War and the Lahore Declaration
Control over India’s economic liberalisation programme
accepted.x: Food aid, the Soviet veto on Kashmir and support over Goa contributed to warmer India-Soviet relations after the Korean War.
accepted.tq: Select the option containing the complete set of stated causes.
accepted.sec: Nehruvian era - NAM, Korean War role, 1962 impact

accepted.s: The 1962 war with China demonstrated the limits of:
accepted.x: The 1962 war with China exposed the limitations of the idealist approach associated with the early Nehruvian phase.
accepted.tq: Link the historical shock to the policy approach it challenged.
accepted.sec: Nehruvian era - NAM, Korean War role, 1962 impact

accepted.s: The phase of Indian foreign policy from 1962 to 1971 was characterised as:
accepted.x: The 1962–1971 phase was described as realism and recovery, including defence build-up, the 1965 war, Tashkent and refusal to sign the NPT.
accepted.tq: Match the period with its precise phase title.
accepted.sec: Nehruvian era - NAM, Korean War role, 1962 impact

accepted.s:
Which of the following developments belonged to the 1962–1971 phase of realism and recovery?
1. Defence build-up
2. Tashkent Declaration of 1966
3. Refusal to sign the NPT in 1968
4. NSG waiver of 2008
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: Defence build-up, the 1965 war and Tashkent, and refusal to sign the NPT belonged to the 1962–1971 phase. The NSG waiver came in 2008.
accepted.tq: Reject a later nuclear-development milestone from an earlier historical phase.
accepted.sec: Nehruvian era - NAM, Korean War role, 1962 impact

accepted.s: India was criticised for taking the Kashmir issue to the United Nations in:
accepted.x: The decision to take Kashmir to the United Nations in January 1948 was a subject of criticism in assessments of India’s foreign policy.
accepted.tq: Recall the specific month and year associated with the criticism.
accepted.sec: Nehruvian era - NAM, Korean War role, 1962 impact

accepted.s: The period 1991–1998 was described as the phase of:
accepted.x: The 1991–1998 phase focused on safeguarding strategic autonomy after the collapse of the USSR and the 1991 economic crisis.
accepted.tq: Match the phase label with both its period and historical context.

accepted.s: The Look East Policy was launched in 1991–1992 under:
accepted.x: The Look East Policy was launched in 1991–1992 under Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao and brought India closer to ASEAN.
accepted.tq: Apply the wrong-person-with-the-deed trap to a foreign-policy initiative.

accepted.s: A major objective and outcome of the Look East Policy was to:
o: End India’s relations with West Asia
Replace the Commonwealth with a military alliance
Create a common currency with the Soviet Union
accepted.x: The Look East Policy moved India closer to ASEAN and strengthened engagement with East and Southeast Asia.
accepted.tq: Identify the regional direction of the policy rather than its domestic economic context.

accepted.s: Which of the following best explains the foreign-policy significance of LPG reforms?
o: India abandoned all economic engagement with other countries
India replaced economic diplomacy with military diplomacy
India made membership of a Cold War bloc its principal objective
Attracting foreign direct investment and markets became foreign-policy goals
accepted.x: Liberalisation, privatisation and globalisation reforms made attracting FDI and accessing markets important foreign-policy goals.
accepted.tq: Connect a domestic economic reform process with its external-policy effect.
accepted.sec: Post-Cold War shifts - Look East, economic diplomacy, West Asia

accepted.s: Strategic ties between India and the United States began to develop during the:
accepted.x: Strategic ties with the United States began developing during the unipolar moment extending from 1991 to 2008.
accepted.tq: Use the stated period boundaries to distinguish successive foreign-policy phases.

accepted.s: India established full diplomatic relations with Israel in 1992 while:
o: Joining a military alliance led by Israel
Maintaining ties with the Arab world
Severing all relations with West Asian countries
Suspending economic diplomacy with the United States
accepted.x: India established full diplomatic relations with Israel in 1992 while continuing to maintain ties with the Arab world.
accepted.tq: Recognise the simultaneous pursuit of relations with Israel and Arab countries.

accepted.s: The Gujral Doctrine of 1996 emphasised:
o: Military intervention in neighbouring countries without consultation
Balancing every concession with an immediate reciprocal demand
Goodwill towards neighbours without asking for anything in return
accepted.x: The Gujral Doctrine advocated goodwill towards neighbouring countries without expecting immediate reciprocity.
accepted.tq: Distinguish unilateral goodwill from reciprocal bargaining.

accepted.x: The phase termed regional assertion was associated with India becoming the leading power in South Asia.
